name: Second Chance Welding
old_description: We Provide Professional Solutions To Deliver Safe & Efficient Projects
about:
Second Chance Welding operates from a shop in Johnston, Rhode Island. The business is owned by Andrew Quinn, who holds certifications across a range of material thicknesses. The company focuses on giving vehicles and equipment a second chance through certified automotive rust repair, fabrication, and structural steel welding.

The shop provides rust repair, welding, and fabrication services, including structural steel welding and mobile welding at customer sites. Work is performed at a shop rate of $100 per hour plus materials, with a mobile rate of $125 per hour plus materials. Minimum charges apply: $100 for shop jobs under one hour and $500 for mobile jobs under four hours. All estimates are free and offered Monday through Friday from 3 p.m. to 5 p.m., with no estimates on Wednesdays or Saturdays unless by appointment.

Customers include automotive owners and operators of heavy equipment needing rust repair or custom fabrication. The shop accepts money orders, certified bank checks, and major credit cards with a 4% processing fee; personal checks are not accepted. Completed vehicles or parts must be retrieved within 48 hours to avoid a $25-per-day storage fee.

The company’s stated mission is to deliver professional solutions that ensure safe and efficient projects, emphasizing the owner’s certification in every material thickness as a key differentiator.

name: Second Sunrise Solar
old_description: The average home can save between $10,000 and $30,000 over the lifetime of your solar panel system.
about:
Second Sunrise Solar operates from Mt Pleasant, South Carolina. The company describes itself as a family-run business, though its founding year and founders are not publicly disclosed.

The firm provides full-service solar photovoltaic installation for residential and commercial customers. Its scope covers initial consultation, system design, financing assistance, permitting, installation, grid interconnection, and ongoing monitoring. In addition to solar, the company performs Gold Star Certified Building Performance Institute (BPI) energy audits and installs efficiency upgrades such as insulation, air and duct sealing, smart thermostats, radiant barriers, solar attic fans, LED lighting, and hybrid water heaters. No facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures are published.

The customer base includes homeowners and businesses across the company’s service area. Reviews cite projects for individual residences and note commercial-scale installations, though specific client names are not disclosed.

Second Sunrise Solar emphasizes a “full service” model that keeps every step in-house, a 25-year parts and production warranty on panels, racking, and inverters, and an 10-year workmanship warranty. The company says it began each project with a BPI energy audit to maximize overall energy and financial savings.

name: Seed Solar Denver
about:
Seed Solar Denver operates from its headquarters in Denver, Colorado, serving the Front Range and broader state. The company describes itself as a Colorado-born, locally owned and operated crew founded to change the solar industry one installation at a time, rejecting the high-pressure sales and delayed timelines common among national conglomerates.

The firm provides end-to-end residential and commercial energy solutions without subcontractors. Services span custom solar design and installation, battery storage (Tesla Powerwall and Enphase systems), panel detach-and-reset for roof replacements, main panel upgrades to 200-amp service, EV charger installation, heat pump deployment, roofing, system diagnostics and repairs, and critter guard fitting. Commercial work includes rooftop, carport, and ground-mount arrays plus community-scale solar farm development. Seed Solar manages design, permitting, HOA approvals, and utility interconnection—primarily with Xcel Energy—and backs installations with a 10-year workmanship warranty.

Customers range from homeowners seeking tailored solar and storage systems to businesses aiming to cut operating costs and meet sustainability targets, plus developers building ground-mounted community solar projects. The company emphasizes local expertise with Colorado weather, roofing styles, and regulatory processes.

Seed Solar says its differentiation lies in owning the entire process, employing craftsmen who treat each home with respect, offering honest pricing without aggressive sales tactics, and maintaining a local presence that ensures accountability.

name: Select Technology Inc
old_description: We will serve you as a valuable link in your supply chain, offering worldwide access to OEM, CEM and distributor inventories.
about:
Select Technology Inc is based in Rowley, Massachusetts, where it operates as an independent stocking distributor of electronic components. The company serves as a link in the supply chain, offering worldwide access to OEM, contract electronics manufacturer (CEM), and distributor inventories.

The distributor maintains over 10,000 line items in its on-site inventory and provides a range of value-added services including bill-of-materials analysis, microscopic inspection, solderability testing, de-lidding (destructive physical analysis), x-ray analysis, product programming, tape-and-reeling, dry packing, and baking. Its warehouse is fully ESD and MSD compliant per IPC/JEDEC J-STD-033A, and its incoming quality-control team averages 20 years of experience in electronic component inspection.

Select Technology’s customer base includes direct manufacturers and representatives, Fortune 500 OEMs and CEMs, independent distributors, and franchise distributors. The company holds AS9120:2016 certification, indicating a focus on aerospace and defense supply chains, alongside ISO 9001:2015 and ANSI/ESD S20.20-2021.

The company emphasizes its experienced staff—account managers average more than 10 years in electronic distribution—and offers 24/7 availability, a dedicated customer portal for full supply-chain visibility, and a counterfeit prevention process that combines visual inspection, electrical testing, and third-party laboratory analysis. Same-day shipping is available for stocked parts.

name: SemiProbe
old_description: The SemiProbe Wafer Prober Platform is Easily Configurable to Adapt to Many Applications Over the Life of the Prober
about:
SemiProbe is headquartered in Winooski, Vermont. The company designs and manufactures wafer probing systems in the United States. No founding year or ownership details are publicly disclosed.

SemiProbe produces the Probe System for Life (PS4L) family of probing and inspection platforms, built on a patented adaptive architecture that makes components interchangeable, configurable, and field-upgradable. The product line includes complete manipulators, probe arms, probe tips, and automated probing systems for applications such as MEMS, high-frequency/microwave, high-power devices, optoelectronics, photonics, vacuum, double-sided, magnetic stimulation, and device characterization. All systems are designed and manufactured in the USA.

The company serves semiconductor manufacturers, research labs, and device characterization facilities working in MEMS, RF/microwave, power electronics, photonics, and advanced packaging. Customers use SemiProbe systems for wafer-level testing, high-frequency measurement, and automated production probing.

SemiProbe emphasizes modularity and long-term investment value: its PS4L architecture allows users to reconfigure or upgrade probers as test requirements change, avoiding full system replacement. The company states this approach maximizes prober investment value over the life of the equipment.

name: Semicoa
old_description: Manufactures discrete silicon semiconductors for military, aerospace and space customers at its Hawthorne, California site.
about:
Semicoa operates from Hawthorne, California, where it has specialized in discrete silicon semiconductors for more than 50 years. The company focuses on the design, development, and wafer fabrication of high-reliability devices for demanding environments.

Its product line includes bipolar power transistors, small-signal transistors, radiation-hardened devices, and ceramic surface-mount diodes. Semicoa performs discrete and hybrid assembly on dedicated high-volume lines, leveraging proprietary scalable processes that integrate with foundry partners. The facility provides in-house environmental and life testing per MIL-PRF-19500, including radiation lot acceptance, real-time X-ray, PIND testing, and fine/gross leak testing with Krypton 85.

The company serves military, aerospace, space, and defense customers worldwide. Its components have been used in smallsat programs, spacecraft, and other mission-critical systems where failure is not an option. Semicoa supports qualified parts lists (QPL) and source control drawings (SCDs) with full traceability to wafer and diffusion runs.

Semicoa differentiates itself through the highest U.S. government qualification (JANS level per MIL-PRF-19500) and certifications to AS9100D and ISO 9001:2015. Its modular process development, custom packaging and plating options, and comprehensive documentation capabilities are designed to meet the stringent requirements of space-level applications.

about:
Semiconductor Processing Co. (SPC) has operated from Boston, Massachusetts since its founding in 1967. The company occupies a facility in the city's Seaport district, where it has provided precision wafer manufacturing services for over four decades. No information about the founders or ownership structure is publicly disclosed.

SPC specializes in the production of Silicon on Insulator (SOI) and Germanium on Insulator (GeOI) wafers, offering substrate bonding services and 200 mm wafer processing. Its equipment lineup includes a production bonder for SOI and direct wafer bonding, a scanning acoustic microscope, an MRL dual horizontal tube furnace, and various ADE gauges for metrology. The company does not publish facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures.

The business serves the semiconductor industry, supplying engineered wafers to device manufacturers and research organizations. The website does not name specific customers or end markets beyond the general wafer manufacturing sector.

The company emphasizes its long track record in precision wafer manufacturing, dating back to 1967, but does not articulate a specific founding mission or competitive differentiation beyond its technical capabilities.

name: Semiconductor Support Services, Co
old_description: Our mission is to partner with our customers and enable them to sustain and improve their operations, using our high quality services and products.
about:
Semiconductor Support Services, Co. (SSSco) was established in 2001 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas. The company operates as a privately held business serving the semiconductor manufacturing sector.

SSSco provides a range of services and products focused on wafer fabrication equipment. Its offerings include equipment repairs, upgrades, and retrofits, along with on-site support and training. The company maintains a large inventory of OEM and equivalent spare parts for systems from Applied Materials (AMAT), MKS, SMC, Lam Research, and Tokyo Electron (TEL). SSSco also develops and sells its own Penulator™ product family, which includes remote, data, video, and single-board computer (SBC) modules designed to improve equipment efficiency and address obsolescence. A repair center and upgrade center support these activities.

The company serves semiconductor fabs and equipment owners who operate AMAT Endura, Centura, and Producer platforms, among others. Specific project examples cited by SSSco include HP/HP+ robot driver upgrades, EPI and Poly SCR driver upgrades, and AMAT MUX PCB repairs. Customers range from chipmakers seeking productivity gains to those needing obsolescence solutions for legacy tools.

SSSco states its mission is to partner with customers to sustain and improve their operations through high-quality services and products. The company emphasizes rapid response with the tagline "When it has to be right…now," reflecting a focus on minimizing downtime for critical fab equipment.

name: Seneca Foods Corporation
old_description: At Seneca, we produce seeds, harvest crops, manufacture our own containers, and provide a wide range of nutritious fruit and vegetable products.
about:
Seneca Foods Corporation, founded in 1949 in Ripon, Wisconsin, is a publicly traded, vertically integrated fruit and vegetable processing company. The business began with a focus on producing seeds, harvesting crops, manufacturing its own containers, and delivering a wide range of nutritious fruit and vegetable products to market.

The company operates a fully integrated model, managing seed production, crop harvesting from over 1,400 family farms, container manufacturing, and processing of fruit and vegetable products. Its portfolio includes well-known brands such as Green Giant, Aunt Nellie's, Libby's, CherryMan, Read Salads, Green Valley, and Seneca Snacks. Seneca emphasizes food safety through seven major quality systems and invests in technology for its state-of-the-art facilities across multiple plant locations.

Seneca serves the food industry by supplying branded and private-label fruit and vegetable products to retailers, foodservice operators, and food manufacturers. The company's vertically integrated supply chain allows it to control quality from seed to shelf, providing consistent products such as sweet peas, cherries, and cannellini beans to meet organizational needs.

The company differentiates itself through its "Farm Fresh Goodness Made Great" philosophy, long-standing grower relationships, and commitment to food safety, environmental stewardship, and conservative financial management. Seneca's fundamental beliefs—honesty, accountability, and respect for growers and employees—have guided its operations since 1949, fostering long-term employee loyalty and shareholder value.

name: SenseICs Corporation
old_description: SenseICs is dedicated to reimagining the status quo, designing and building next-generation integrated circuits, and delivering the best possible solutions to meet the needs of our customers.
about:
SenseICs Corporation is based in Columbus, Ohio The company was co-founded by Ramy Tantawy, PhD, and Dale Shane Smith, PhD. Both bring decades of mixed-signal integrated circuit design experience from Intel, Micron, Forza Silicon, and Ohio State University's Electroscience Lab. The founding year is not publicly disclosed.

As a fabless semiconductor provider, SenseICs designs and develops silicon-verified integrated circuits and microelectronics hardware. Its core technologies include high dynamic range readout integrated circuits (HDR ROICs), tamper-resistant ICs, and wide-band gallium nitride power amplifiers. The company offers full turnkey services from design and tape-out through packaging and test, and supplies evaluation hardware and development kits. Fabrication is typically conducted via multi-project wafer runs with foundry partners such as SkyWater, GlobalFoundries, Tower Semiconductor, and onsemi.

SenseICs serves high-energy physics experiments, medical imaging electronics, and defense and commercial markets. Its customer base includes NASA, the U.S. Navy, Air Force, Army Research Laboratory, CERN, Jefferson Lab, and academic partners at The Ohio State University. The company collaborates closely with OSU's ElectroScience Laboratory, Nanotech West Lab, and Department of Physics.

The company emphasizes a multidisciplinary approach and a culture summarized by the acronym STRIDE (Staying Curious, Trust, Resilience, Innovation, Diversity, Excellence). It positions its differentiation on radiation-hardening by design for environments exceeding 100 Mrad total ionizing dose, microelectronics, and a team with deep expertise in mixed-signal IC design, RF, and high-speed communication.
